goals.description: Determine which Docker workflow is relevant, inspect available Dockerfile, compose files, project manifests, environment examples, ignore files, and infer runtime, services, dependencies, ports, and production constraints.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on context gathering only. Identify the user's requested Docker task type: optimization, compose generation/improvement, security audit, or a combination. Read relevant Dockerfile, docker-compose files, project manifests, .dockerignore, .gitignore, and environment examples. Infer language/framework, build artifacts, services, ports, dependency files, and production/runtime needs before making changes.
goals.name: Gather Docker context

goals.description: Inspect the Dockerfile for base image choice, tag pinning, layer count, package manager cache handling, dependency-copy order, multi-stage usage, .dockerignore coverage, and common optimization anti-patterns.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on Dockerfile analysis. Read the current Dockerfile and identify its base image, tag specificity, approximate image-size implications, layer count from RUN/COPY/ADD, cache-busting order, missing .dockerignore patterns, package-cache retention, missing multi-stage separation, and other optimization anti-patterns. Do not rewrite yet except to note concrete required changes.
goals.name: Analyze Dockerfile baseline

goals.description: Select appropriate pinned runtime bases and apply or improve multi-stage build structure so build tools, source code, and development dependencies are excluded from the final image.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on base image and multi-stage structure. Replace unsuitable or :latest bases with specific slim/alpine/distroless/scratch choices that match runtime needs. Add or refine builder/runtime stages where appropriate, separate build dependencies from runtime dependencies, and ensure the final stage copies only required artifacts.
goals.name: Optimize base image and stages

goals.description: Reorder dependency and source-copy layers, combine related RUN instructions, clean package-manager caches in the same layer, add BuildKit cache mounts when useful, and create or update .dockerignore.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on layer and cache behavior. Put dependency manifests before application source copies, install dependencies in their own cacheable layers, avoid early COPY . ., combine related RUN commands with cleanup in the same layer, use BuildKit cache mounts where appropriate, and ensure .dockerignore excludes files such as .git, node_modules, __pycache__, .env, build outputs, and other unnecessary context.
goals.name: Optimize layers and build cache

goals.description: Add concise inline comments for non-obvious Dockerfile decisions and prepare an estimate or qualitative summary of expected size and build-performance improvements.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on explanation and reporting for the optimized Dockerfile. Add inline comments only where they clarify important decisions, such as stage boundaries, cache optimization, non-root user setup, or base-image choice. Summarize the likely image-size and build-cache improvements without overclaiming exact measurements unless measured.
goals.name: Document optimized Dockerfile decisions

goals.description: Run or recommend the Dockerfile analyzer validation and address relevant findings from the optimized Dockerfile.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on Dockerfile validation. Run `python3 scripts/dockerfile_analyzer.py Dockerfile` if the tool exists and execution is available. Review analyzer output for remaining optimization, multi-stage, layer, or security findings. Fix actionable issues within the Dockerfile scope, or report any validation that could not be run.
goals.name: Validate Dockerfile

goals.description: Infer compose services such as app, workers, databases, caches, queues, and reverse proxies, including their dependencies, ports, persistent data, and environment needs.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on service identification for docker-compose. Determine which services are needed or already present: web/API, workers, databases, cache, queue, reverse proxy, and supporting infrastructure. Capture dependencies, health endpoints or commands, exposed ports, volumes, environment variables, and development versus production requirements.
goals.name: Identify compose service topology

goals.description: Create or improve compose service definitions with pinned images, healthchecks, depends_on health conditions, resource limits, restart policy where appropriate, and production-safe service settings.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on compose service definitions. Add or improve services with pinned image versions or build blocks, healthchecks for every service, `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` where supported, resource limits such as memory and CPU, and appropriate restart behavior for production. Keep service definitions aligned with the inferred project topology.
goals.name: Configure compose services

goals.description: Define explicit frontend/backend networks, restrict external port exposure, mark backend-only networks internal, and use named volumes for persistent data.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on compose networking and persistence. Replace reliance on the default network with explicit networks, separate frontend and backend traffic where useful, expose only ports that need host access, use `internal: true` for backend-only networks, and configure named volumes for database or other persistent data.
goals.name: Configure compose networks and volumes

goals.description: Move secrets to env files, generate .env.example documentation, ensure .env is ignored, use variable substitution defaults, and annotate development versus production profiles or overrides.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on compose environment handling and dev/prod separation. Use `env_file` and variable substitution instead of committing secrets inline. Generate or update `.env.example` documenting required variables, ensure `.env` is in `.gitignore`, and use compose profiles or override-file conventions for dev hot reload/debug ports versus production-safe settings.
goals.name: Configure compose environment and profiles

goals.description: Run or recommend compose validation and address relevant findings about service dependencies, healthchecks, networks, volumes, environment variables, and ports.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on compose validation. Run `python3 scripts/compose_validator.py docker-compose.yml` if available, and optionally Docker Compose config validation if appropriate. Check for missing healthchecks, dependency issues, network mistakes, volume problems, inline secrets, and port conflicts. Fix actionable compose issues or report validation limitations.
goals.name: Validate compose configuration

goals.description: Check Dockerfile security issues including root user, latest tags, secrets in ENV or ARG, broad COPY patterns, unnecessary EXPOSE, missing HEALTHCHECK, privileged patterns, and retained package caches.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on Dockerfile security audit. Check for running as root, use of `:latest`, secrets in ENV/ARG, broad or unsafe COPY/ADD, missing or unnecessary HEALTHCHECK/EXPOSE, privileged assumptions, retained package-manager caches, and missing non-root user creation. Record severity and concrete fix recommendations.
goals.name: Audit Dockerfile security

goals.description: Check compose or runtime container settings for root execution, writable root filesystem, retained capabilities, missing resource limits, host networking, sensitive mounts, and missing log limits.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on runtime security audit. Inspect docker-compose or available runtime configuration for containers running as root, writable root filesystems, missing `cap_drop`, absent memory/CPU limits, host network mode, sensitive mounts such as `/var/run/docker.sock`, and missing logging size limits. Record severity and concrete fix recommendations.
goals.name: Audit runtime security

goals.description: Summarize container security findings with severity counts and detailed remediation recommendations in the prescribed audit-report format.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on the final security report. Produce a `SECURITY AUDIT` summary with timestamp or current date if available, counts for Critical, High, Medium, and Low findings, and detailed findings with actionable fixes. Keep Dockerfile findings and runtime/compose findings clear and separate.
goals.name: Produce security report
